data.title: Govern the public evidence boundary as one shared contract
data.context: CallerSignal now serves rights-approved numbering and complaint evidence through CLI, MCP, HTTP, web, and Vercel. Changes to sources, schemas, trust boundaries, privacy minimization, or assessment semantics can create public safety and data-rights consequences across every surface.
data.decision: Treat the rights-approved source-to-assessment pipeline and its public surfaces as one governed architecture scope. Keep normalization, evidence, assessment, and transparency contracts shared; isolate source ingestion and deployment behind explicit adapters; keep raw data, secrets, identity claims, lookup demand, and disabled mutation paths outside the public read model.
consequences: Material tasks affecting sources, public schemas, trust boundaries, assessment policy, or deployment data must reference the public-evidence-platform brief and record architecture conformance.
Every enabled source must retain machine-validated authority, permitted fields, provenance, freshness, minimization, outage, correction, and takedown controls.
CLI, MCP, HTTP, and web may adapt transport and presentation but cannot create independent evidence or verdict logic.
Future report storage, identity verification, licensed vendors, and mutation infrastructure require separate decisions when selected.
